cityWatch.label: CITY WATCH
cityWatch.text: Karnataka says half-helmet restrictions and taxi fare meters are planned before the New Year, with penalties also rising for footpath riding.

lead.headline: KARNATAKA TO BAN HALF-HELMETS AND REQUIRE METERS IN APP-BASED TAXIS
lead.deck: The transport minister says the helmet ban will be enforced before the New Year; Ola and Uber taxis will also have to use government-fixed fares, while footpath-riding fines are set to rise.
paragraphs: Karnataka is preparing to ban half-helmets for two-wheeler riders, with enforcement expected before the end of 2026, Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh said in Bengaluru on Monday.
The state is also preparing rules requiring all taxis, including app-based cabs such as Ola and Uber, to install meters and charge government-fixed fares. Violations will attract penalties.

Fines for riding two-wheelers on footpaths are set to double to ₹5,000 for a first offence and ₹10,000 for a second; a third offence could lead to vehicle seizure. The government has also paused new Green SM taxi registrations after 100 vehicles were registered.

sidebarStory.headline: MAN SHOT DEAD AFTER GUNMEN FIRE MORE THAN 20 ROUNDS NEAR MINISTER’S OFFICE
sidebarStory.subhead: Police and forensic teams reached the scene after the shooting near the office of Delhi minister Kapil Mishra; investigators are examining evidence.
paragraphs: A man was killed when gunmen fired more than 20 rounds near the office of Delhi minister Kapil Mishra, according to a PTI report carried by NDTV early Tuesday.
Police teams, a crime team and a forensic science laboratory team were sent to collect evidence. The investigation is continuing.

stories.headline: DELIVERY WORKER BEATEN TO DEATH BY FRIEND AFTER LATE-NIGHT SPAT IN KORAMANGALA
paragraphs: A 35-year-old delivery worker, Shivakumar, was allegedly beaten to death with a stick by a friend after an argument near a paan shop in Koramangala First Block late Sunday night.
Police are investigating the killing; the report said the two men had argued over abusive language.

stories.headline: BENGALURU TECH SUMMIT OPENS WITH AI, DEEPTECH AND ROBOTICS IN FOCUS
paragraphs: The three-day Bengaluru Tech Summit begins Tuesday at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre under the theme “AI & Beyond.”
Organisers expect more than 10,000 delegates, 700 speakers and 1,500 exhibitors from over 65 countries, with an AI and Robotics Pavilion among the major draws.

stories.source: The Week / Press Trust of India
stories.headline: KARNATAKA PLANS DEDICATED BENGALURU UNIT TO TACKLE GANGS AND DRUG CRIME
paragraphs: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar said the state is setting up a separate anti-rowdy squad under Bengaluru’s police commissionerate to tackle criminal activity and drug-related offences.
The unit is intended to operate independently of local police stations, according to the report.

stories.headline: SIX NAGA MEN KIDNAPPED AND KILLED IN MANIPUR LAID TO REST AFTER 187 DAYS
paragraphs: The six men, from the Liangmai/Zeliangrong Naga community, were buried on Monday, 187 days after they were kidnapped from Leilon Vaiphei village in Manipur’s Kangpokpi district.
Their bodies were recovered on June 10. The burial followed separate communications from community groups and Ladakh Police, NDTV reported.

stories.headline: INDIA FACES AIRCRAFT SHORTAGE; READY TO ORDER 1,000 MORE PLANES, SAYS GOYAL
paragraphs: India is facing an acute shortage of civilian aircraft and is prepared to order 1,000 more planes to meet air-traffic demand, Union minister Piyush Goyal said Monday.
He said the government is pursuing established manufacturers for faster deliveries as Indian carriers work through large aircraft orders.

stories.headline: AKVAN EXPECTED TO INTENSIFY INTO SEVERE CYCLONE; EAST COAST STATES ALERTED
paragraphs: Cyclone Akvan is intensifying over the Bay of Bengal, with the India Meteorological Department warning of winds up to 130 kmph and gusts up to 145 kmph as it approaches the Andhra Pradesh coast.
Authorities in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha are on alert as the storm strengthens; residents should follow official weather and evacuation advisories.

stories.headline: PUBLISHER ARRESTED IN TAMIL NADU LIBRARY BOOKS PROCUREMENT SCAM
paragraphs: Publisher R Mohan has been arrested over alleged irregularities in the procurement of books for Tamil Nadu libraries, NDTV reported Tuesday.
Investigators allege that books were created under fictitious authors’ names using material sourced from websites and online platforms. The case follows questions raised about the procurement.

stories.headline: NEW DAILY KANPUR–DELHI EXPRESS TO BOOST RAIL CONNECTIVITY
paragraphs: Indian Railways is adding a daily express service between Kanpur and Delhi, with Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw set to flag off the train.
The route links Uttar Pradesh’s industrial hub with the national capital; the service is intended to improve rail connectivity for passengers.

stories.headline: ODISHA TRIBALS THREATEN PROTEST AFTER SACRED-SITE DISPUTE
paragraphs: Tribal groups in Odisha have threatened a protest after an incident at a sacred site linked to allegations of cow slaughter, The Indian Express reported Monday.
The Biju Janata Dal has backed the planned protest, while the Vishwa Hindu Parishad criticised the arrest of five Bajrang Dal activists over the October incident.

stories.headline: EARTHSHOT AWARDS DEBUT IN INDIA AS WILLIAM AND CATHERINE VISIT MUMBAI
paragraphs: Prince William and Princess Catherine are in Mumbai for the three-day India visit, with the 2026 Earthshot Prize awards ceremony scheduled for Tuesday evening.
The environmental awards are being hosted in India for the first time. The couple began the visit Monday with community engagements, including a street-cricket game in Ballard Estate.

stories.headline: WOMEN PARLIAMENTARIANS’ CONFERENCE OPENS IN BENGALURU
listing: The two-day women parliamentarians’ conference begins today at Vidhana Soudha.

stories.headline: MORNING MIST IN BENGALURU; NO CITY WARNING IN FORCE

paragraphs: The IMD forecast for Bengaluru on Tuesday is mist, with a minimum of 17°C and maximum of 29°C. No warning is in force.
